title: Sell Mineral Rights in Forestdale, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Forestdale, AL
metaDescription: Forestdale, Jefferson County mineral owner sitting on an old coal-era severance? We buy Black Warrior Basin interests with a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Forestdale is unincorporated Jefferson County, and a surprising number of the mineral titles here still trace back to land the coal companies carved up before the community was ever platted as a subdivision.
intro: We hear a version of the same story from Forestdale owners often: a parent or grandparent kept the surface, or sold the surface but kept a fraction of the minerals, and nobody in the family has thought about it since, until a small royalty check or a landman's letter showed up.

sections.heading: Reading a Forestdale royalty statement
paragraphs: If you are receiving a statement, look at the operator name first. Diversified Energy runs a large share of the legacy Black Warrior coalbed methane wells that were originally drilled by Energen, and their statements list gross production, your decimal interest, and deductions before the net check amount. That decimal is what any buyer, including us, will use to size an offer.

If the check has gone quiet or dropped to almost nothing, that usually means the well is at the tail of its decline curve, which is a normal life stage for coal-gas wells in this basin, not a sign anything is wrong with your title.

sections.heading: Selling a fractional interest
paragraphs: Most Forestdale interests we buy are small fractions inherited alongside several cousins or siblings. You do not need everyone to agree. We can buy just your undivided share and let the rest of the family decide separately what they want to do.
We start with the legal description on your deed or the operator's division order, confirm current production, and put a number in front of you within a few business days.

sections.heading: What we look for before we quote
paragraphs: Current operator and well status, your net royalty decimal, whether the interest is producing or held by production nearby, and whether title passed cleanly through probate. Anything unusual, like a lease that expired years ago with no current well, we flag honestly rather than pretend it is worth more than it is.

faqs.question: My Forestdale check is only a few dollars a month. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: Small monthly checks add up to a modest lump sum, and for many owners that lump sum is more useful than years of small deposits. We will give you a real number so you can decide.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests with no current production?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if there is a history of production nearby or the tract sits inside an active unit. We are upfront when an interest is too speculative for us to make an offer worth your time.

faqs.question: Who is the typical operator in this area?
faqs.answer: Diversified Energy operates most of the legacy CBM wells in western Jefferson County today, following its purchase of Energen's Black Warrior Basin coalbed methane assets.

faqs.question: How do you value my fraction?
faqs.answer: We start from your net decimal interest, recent production history, and typical hold periods for wells at this stage of decline, and quote against what recent royalty checks actually show.
